ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle RST, with a right-angle mark at point S, so ∠S = 90°. Side RT continues past point T and is extended to point P, and at point T, the exterior angle formed by ray TS and the extension TP is marked as 150°. Reasoning: The interior angle ∠RTS of the triangle at point T and the marked 150° exterior angle form a pair of linear angles, so ∠T = 180° - 150° = 30°. In right triangle RST, the sum of the interior angles of the triangle is 180°, therefore ∠R = 180° - 90° - 30° = 60°.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as triangle RST with a right-angle marker at S, and with side RT extended past T to point P. The marked 150° angle is the exterior angle at T formed by TS and the extension TP. Since the interior angle at T and the 150° exterior angle form a linear pair, compute angle T as 180° - 150° = 30°. From the text, the target is m∠R in right triangle RST; using the triangle angle sum with ∠S = 90° gives ∠R = 180° - 90° - 30° = 60°.
